subject: Geography
description: Sahara, Nile, Great Rift Valley, Atlas, Congo, capitals, key features

questions.stem: The world's LARGEST hot DESERT, located in northern Africa, is the:

options.option_text: Kalahari, in southern Africa region
Sahara, spanning much of north Africa
Namib, on the south-west Atlantic coast
Atacama, in coastal western South America

questions.explanation: Sahara — largest hot desert (~9.2 million km², roughly the size of the continental US). Spans 11 countries — Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Western Sahara, Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Chad, Sudan. Largest desert overall is ANTARCTICA (cold desert, ~14 million km²). Distractor 1 = Kalahari (southern Africa). Distractor 3 = Namib (Namibia, Atlantic coast). Distractor 4 = Atacama (driest desert, Chile/Peru).

questions.stem: The LONGEST river in Africa (and one of the longest in the world) is the:

options.option_text: Congo River, of central African basin
Nile River, flowing through 11 African countries
Niger River, of west African region
Zambezi River, of southern African region

questions.explanation: Nile — ~6,650 km. Often listed as the LONGEST river in the world (Amazon contests this; modern measurements suggest Amazon may be longer). Two main tributaries: WHITE NILE (origin Lake Victoria; primary source) + BLUE NILE (origin Lake Tana, Ethiopia; carries most sediment + water during rains). Joins at Khartoum, Sudan; flows through Egypt; delta at Mediterranean. Civilisations along Nile — Ancient Egypt, Nubia. Aswan High Dam (1970, USSR-aided, Egypt). Distractor 1 = Congo (~4,700 km, 2nd longest). Distractor 3 = Niger (~4,180 km). Distractor 4 = Zambezi (~2,693 km).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The GREAT RIFT VALLEY, a major geological feature, runs through:

options.option_text: Western Africa, from Senegal to Nigeria
Eastern Africa, from Mozambique to the Red Sea
Northern Africa, across the Sahara region
Southern Africa, around the Cape of Good Hope

questions.explanation: East African Rift — ~6,400 km long, from Mozambique through Malawi, Tanzania, Kenya, Ethiopia, into the Red Sea + Jordan Valley. Caused by Africa SPLITTING into two tectonic plates (Nubian + Somali) at ~6-7 mm/year — eventually a new ocean will form (millions of years). Hosts the AFRICAN GREAT LAKES — Tanganyika, Malawi, Turkana, Albert. Active volcanoes — Kilimanjaro, Kenya, Nyiragongo. Hominid fossil sites — Olduvai Gorge (Tanzania), Hadar (Ethiopia, Lucy). Distractors are wrong regions.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The HIGHEST MOUNTAIN in Africa is:

options.option_text: Mount Kenya, in the country of Kenya
Mount Kilimanjaro, in northern Tanzania
Mount Stanley, in the Rwenzori range
Mount Cameroon, in west African Cameroon

questions.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro — Tanzania, 5,895 m. Africa's highest peak; one of the SEVEN SUMMITS. Stratovolcano with three cones (Kibo, Mawenzi, Shira). Snow-capped summit (icecap shrinking due to climate change). Largest free-standing mountain in the world (rises ~5 km from surrounding plains). Distractor 1 = Mount Kenya (5,199 m, 2nd highest). Distractor 3 = Mt Stanley / Margherita Peak (Rwenzori, Uganda-DRC, 5,109 m, 3rd). Distractor 4 = Mount Cameroon (4,040 m, active volcano).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The largest country in Africa by AREA is:

options.option_text: Egypt, of north African region
Algeria, of north-west Africa
South Africa, of southernmost Africa
Nigeria, of west African region

questions.explanation: ALGERIA — ~2.38 million km², largest African country by area (since SUDAN was split into Sudan + South Sudan in 2011 — Sudan was previously largest). 11th largest in world. Capital ALGIERS. Most of Algeria is Sahara desert; population concentrated along Mediterranean coast. Distractor 1 — Egypt (~1 million km², 30th in world). Distractor 3 — South Africa (~1.22 million km²). Distractor 4 — Nigeria (~924,000 km²) but POPULATION largest in Africa (~225 million). Most populous African country = Nigeria.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: VICTORIA FALLS, one of the world's largest waterfalls, lies on the border between:

options.option_text: Egypt and Sudan, on the Nile River
Zambia and Zimbabwe, on the Zambezi River
Kenya and Uganda, between two lakes
Nigeria and Cameroon, on the Niger River

questions.explanation: Victoria Falls — on the ZAMBEZI river, ZAMBIA-ZIMBABWE border. Local name 'Mosi-oa-Tunya' = 'The Smoke that Thunders'. Width 1,708 m, height 108 m. Discovered + named (after Queen Victoria) by David Livingstone in 1855. Volume: 1 km wide × 100 m high curtain of water — among world's largest by combined width × height. UNESCO World Heritage Site. Compare: Niagara (US-Canada, 51 m high but high volume), Iguazu (Brazil-Argentina, ~80 m, very wide), Angel Falls (Venezuela, world's tallest at 979 m).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The country at the southern tip of Africa is:

options.option_text: Madagascar, the large island east of Africa
South Africa, with Cape of Good Hope
Mozambique, on the south-east coast
Namibia, on the south-west coast

questions.explanation: South Africa — southernmost mainland country. Three capitals (unique): PRETORIA (executive), CAPE TOWN (legislative), BLOEMFONTEIN (judicial). CAPE OF GOOD HOPE (south of Cape Town, near Cape Point) — major sailing landmark, named by Bartolomeu Dias (1488). Cape Agulhas — actual southernmost point of African mainland (just east of Cape of Good Hope). Notable geography: Drakensberg mountains; Table Mountain; Kruger NP. Apartheid ended 1994 with Nelson Mandela's election. Distractor 1 — Madagascar is an island. Distractor 3 — Mozambique east coast. Distractor 4 — Namibia is north of South Africa on the west coast.

questions.stem: Which is the largest lake in Africa, shared across three East African nations?

options.option_text: Lake Tanganyika, bordered by DR Congo, Burundi, Tanzania and Zambia
Lake Victoria, shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania
Lake Malawi, lying between Malawi, Tanzania and Mozambique
Lake Chad, bordering Nigeria, Niger, Chad and Cameroon

questions.explanation: Lake Victoria (about 68,800 sq km) is the largest lake in Africa by surface area, shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. Lake Tanganyika is deeper and longer but smaller in surface area — a common confusion. Lake Chad is shrinking due to climate change and is far smaller today.

questions.stem: Which African country has the highest total population, surpassing all other nations on the continent?

options.option_text: Ethiopia, located in the Horn of East Africa region
Egypt, a North African country straddling the Nile delta
Nigeria, situated in West Africa along the Gulf of Guinea
Democratic Republic of Congo, a large Central African country

questions.explanation: Nigeria, with over 220 million people, is Africa's most populous nation. Ethiopia (around 126 million) is the second most populous — a common mix-up. Egypt (~106 million) and DR Congo (~100 million) rank lower. Nigeria's population is projected to be among the world's top 3 by 2050.

questions.stem: Which cape marks the true geographical southernmost point of the African continent — a fact often confused with a more famous nearby headland?

options.option_text: Cape of Good Hope, a famous rocky headland near Cape Town
Cape Agulhas, located about 150 km southeast of Cape Town
Cape Point, situated within Table Mountain National Park
Cape Guardafui, at the northeastern tip near the Horn of Africa

questions.explanation: Cape Agulhas (34°49'S) is the actual southernmost tip of Africa — it also marks the official boundary between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans. Cape of Good Hope (34°21'S), though more famous, lies slightly further north. This is a classic examiner trap. Cape Guardafui is the easternmost point of Africa, not the southernmost.

questions.stem: The 'Sahel' — derived from the Arabic word meaning 'shore' or 'coast' — refers to which geographical zone in Africa?

options.option_text: A coastal mangrove strip running along the Gulf of Guinea shoreline
A semi-arid transitional zone between the Sahara Desert and the tropical savanna
A highland plateau region in the interior of East Africa above 2000 m
A dense equatorial rainforest corridor stretching across Central Africa

questions.explanation: The Sahel is a semi-arid belt stretching east–west across Africa, forming a 'shore' or transition between the Sahara to the north and the wetter savanna to the south. Countries in this zone include Mali, Niger, Chad, Sudan and Burkina Faso. The region is prone to droughts and desertification — topics frequently linked in GK questions. The East African highlands (Option C) are a separate feature.

questions.stem: The Okavango Delta, the world's largest inland river delta and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which country?

options.option_text: Namibia, in the southwestern part of the African continent
Zimbabwe, in its western region near the Hwange National Park
Botswana, in the northwestern Kalahari Desert basin region
Angola, where the Okavango River originates its long journey

questions.explanation: The Okavango Delta forms in Botswana's Kalahari Basin, where the Okavango River — rising in Angola — fans out into a vast inland swamp rather than reaching the sea. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014. Angola is the source of the river (Option D) but the delta itself lies entirely in Botswana. Zimbabwe (Option B) is a common wrong choice due to geographical proximity.

questions.stem: Which African country is estimated to contain MORE ancient pyramids by total count than Egypt, owing to the burial monuments built by its successive Nubian kingdoms?

options.option_text: Ethiopia, where the Aksumite civilisation erected tall granite stelae
Sudan, home to over 200 Meroitic and Kushite pyramids at Meroe and Nuri
Libya, containing ancient Garamantean stone structures in the Fezzan region
Mali, home to the ancient mud-brick mosques and mausoleums of Timbuktu

questions.explanation: Sudan has approximately 200–255 pyramids — more than Egypt's ~138 — built by the Kushite and Meroitic kingdoms between 700 BCE and 350 CE. They are steeper and narrower than Egyptian pyramids. Sites include Meroe, Nuri and El-Kurru. Ethiopia (Option A) is wrong — Aksumite stelae are obelisk-like monoliths, not pyramids. This is a high-frequency exam surprise angle.

questions.stem: Which major river forms the natural international boundary between Zambia and Zimbabwe for a large portion of their shared border?

options.option_text: The Zambezi River, which also plunges over the famous Victoria Falls
The Limpopo River, which flows eastward and drains into Mozambique Channel
The Congo River, notable as the world's deepest river by measured depth
The Orange River, which flows westward and drains into the Atlantic Ocean

questions.explanation: The Zambezi River runs along the Zambia–Zimbabwe border, notably hosting Victoria Falls at that boundary. The Limpopo (Option B) forms South Africa's northern border with Zimbabwe and Botswana — a likely confusion. The Congo River is entirely further north, forming the DR Congo–Republic of Congo border. The Orange River is South Africa's southern boundary with Namibia, draining into the Atlantic.
